## Configuration

### BIND9 Statistics Channel

You must configure BIND9 to enable the statistics channel by adding something similar to the following into your `named.conf`:

```
statistics-channels {
    inet 127.0.0.1 port 8053 allow { 127.0.0.1; };
};
```

See the [BIND9 Administrator Reference Manual](https://bind9.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference.html#statistics-channels-block-grammar) for more details.

### Receiver Config

The following settings are required:

- `endpoint` (default: `http://localhost:8053`): The URL of the BIND9 statistics channel.

The following settings are optional:

- `collection_interval` (default = `10s`): This receiver collects metrics on an interval. This value must be a string readable by Golang's [time.ParseDuration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration). Valid time units are `ns`, `us` (or `µs`), `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`.
- `initial_delay` (default = `1s`): defines how long this receiver waits before starting.

Example:

```yaml
receivers:
  bind9:
    endpoint: "http://localhost:8053"
    collection_interval: 10s
```

## Metrics

The receiver collects the following metrics from the BIND9 statistics channel:

### Server Metrics

| Metric | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `bind9.server.queries` | Total number of incoming DNS queries received by the server, broken down by opcode (QUERY, IQUERY, STATUS, NOTIFY, UPDATE). Collected from the `/json/v1/server` endpoint `opcodes` field. |
| `bind9.server.responses` | Total number of DNS responses sent by the server, broken down by response code (NOERROR, FORMERR, SERVFAIL, NXDOMAIN, NOTIMP, REFUSED, YXDOMAIN, YXRRSET, NXRRSET, NOTAUTH, NOTZONE, BADVERS, BADCOOKIE). Collected from the `/json/v1/server` endpoint `rcodes` field. |

### Resolver Metrics

These metrics are collected per BIND9 view (e.g. `_default`, `_bind`) from the `/json/v1/server` endpoint `views` field.

| Metric | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `bind9.resolver.queries` | Number of outgoing queries made by the resolver, broken down by view and DNS query type (e.g. A, AAAA, NS, DNSKEY). Maps to the `resolver.qtypes` field. |
| `bind9.resolver.responses` | Number of responses received by the resolver, broken down by view. Maps to the `Queryv6` or `Queryv4` value in `resolver.stats`. |
| `bind9.resolver.cache.hits` | Cumulative number of cache hits in the resolver. Maps to `resolver.cachestats.CacheHits`. |
| `bind9.resolver.cache.misses` | Cumulative number of cache misses in the resolver. Maps to `resolver.cachestats.CacheMisses`. |
| `bind9.resolver.cache.entries` | Current number of entries in the resolver cache (gauge). Maps to `resolver.cachestats.CacheNodes`. |
| `bind9.resolver.validation.success` | Cumulative number of successful DNSSEC validations. Maps to `ValOk` in `resolver.stats`. |
| `bind9.resolver.validation.attempt` | Cumulative number of DNSSEC validation attempts. Maps to `ValAttempt` in `resolver.stats`. |

### Memory Metrics

Collected from the `/json/v1/mem` endpoint.

| Metric | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `bind9.memory.total` | Total memory allocated by each named memory context (gauge). Maps to the `total` field per context. |
| `bind9.memory.usage` | Memory currently in use by each named memory context (gauge). Maps to the `inuse` field per context. |

### Network / Socket I/O Metrics

Collected from the `/json/v1/net` endpoint `sockstats` field. All socket metrics are tagged with a `socket.stat` attribute identifying the specific counter (e.g. `UDP4Open`, `TCP6Active`). Socket types are UDP4 (UDP/IPv4), UDP6 (UDP/IPv6), TCP4 (TCP/IPv4), and TCP6 (TCP/IPv6).

| Metric | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `bind9.network.socket.opened` | cumulative sum | Number of sockets opened successfully. Matches counters ending in `Open` (e.g. `UDP4Open`, `TCP6Open`). |
| `bind9.network.socket.open.failures` | cumulative sum | Number of failures to open sockets. Matches counters ending in `OpenFail` (e.g. `UDP4OpenFail`, `TCP6OpenFail`). |
| `bind9.network.socket.closed` | cumulative sum | Number of sockets closed. Matches counters ending in `Close` (e.g. `UDP4Close`, `TCP4Close`). |
| `bind9.network.socket.bind.failures` | cumulative sum | Number of failures to bind sockets. Matches counters ending in `BindFail` (e.g. `UDP4BindFail`, `TCP6BindFail`). |
| `bind9.network.socket.connection` | cumulative sum | Number of connections established successfully. Matches counters ending in `Conn` (e.g. `UDP4Conn`, `TCP4Conn`). |
| `bind9.network.socket.connection.failures` | cumulative sum | Number of failures to connect sockets. Matches counters ending in `ConnFail` (e.g. `UDP4ConnFail`, `TCP6ConnFail`). |
| `bind9.network.socket.accept` | cumulative sum | Number of incoming connections successfully accepted. Only applies to TCP types. Matches counters ending in `Accept` (e.g. `TCP4Accept`, `TCP6Accept`). |
| `bind9.network.socket.accept.failures` | cumulative sum | Number of failures to accept incoming connection requests. Only applies to TCP types. Matches counters ending in `AcceptFail` (e.g. `TCP4AcceptFail`, `TCP6AcceptFail`). |
| `bind9.network.socket.send.errors` | cumulative sum | Number of errors in socket send operations. Matches counters ending in `SendErr` (e.g. `UDP4SendErr`, `TCP6SendErr`). |
| `bind9.network.socket.receive.errors` | cumulative sum | Number of errors in socket receive operations, including errors notified by ICMP error messages on connected UDP sockets. Matches counters ending in `RecvErr` (e.g. `UDP4RecvErr`, `TCP6RecvErr`). |
| `bind9.network.socket.active` | gauge | Number of currently active sockets. Matches counters ending in `Active` (e.g. `UDP4Active`, `TCP6Active`). |

### Traffic Metrics

Collected from the `/json/v1/traffic` endpoint. DNS message size distribution histograms broken down by transport protocol, IP version, and direction.

| Metric | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `bind9.network.traffic` | cumulative sum | DNS message count by size bucket. Each data point has four attributes: `network.transport` (udp/tcp), `network.type` (ipv4/ipv6), `dns.message.direction` (received for incoming requests, sent for outgoing responses), and `dns.message.size.bucket` (e.g. `32-47`, `48-63`). The bucket values represent byte ranges of the DNS messages. |

Attributes on `bind9.network.traffic`:

| Attribute | Description | Values |
|-----------|-------------|--------|
| `network.transport` | Transport protocol | `udp`, `tcp` |
| `network.type` | IP version | `ipv4`, `ipv6` |
| `dns.message.direction` | Message direction | `received` (incoming requests), `sent` (outgoing responses) |
| `dns.message.size.bucket` | Size bucket in bytes | `32-47`, `48-63`, `64-79`, `80-95`, etc. |

For example, a data point with attributes `{network.transport: udp, network.type: ipv4, dns.message.direction: received, dns.message.size.bucket: 32-47}` with value `10` means that 10 UDP/IPv4 DNS request messages were received with a size between 32 and 47 bytes.
